title: Claude Code: Hooks reference
summary: Settings hooks run a shell command, an HTTP request, an MCP tool, a prompt or an agent at lifecycle events: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, Notification, SubagentStart and SubagentStop, TaskCreated and TaskCompleted, Stop, TeammateIdle, PreCompact, SessionEnd and more. Stop and SubagentStop can block the end of a turn (exit 2 sends Claude back to work); PreToolUse can deny or rewrite a call. Only the first 100,000 of about 284,000 characters were read; the per-event input schemas were not.
ideas: A Stop hook can keep an agent working while a gate is open: avenCEO lists this as later.
Notification hooks can route an idle or permission prompt elsewhere.
Settings hooks cannot draw; they gate and add context.
